fraction_of_wage.source: USDOT Office of the Secretary, Departmental Guidance on Valuation of Travel Time in Economic Analysis (1997; Rev.1 2003; Rev.2 2016): local personal travel = 50% of hourly income, plausible range 35-60%
fraction_of_wage.note: Government guidance value (not a student-specific estimate). 'observed' = taken verbatim from published guidance. 2016 PDF host blocked this session; 50% and the 35-60% band confirmed via search extracts of the guidance series.

default_student_wage_usd_h.source: U-M Student Employment Office: $15/h floor for all on-campus temporary and student positions since 2022-08-21 (SEO newsletter fall 2022); Michigan minimum wage $13.73 from 2026-01-01 (michigan.gov/leo), $15.00 from 2027-01-01; postings seen up to ~$18.75
default_student_wage_usd_h.note: Low = state minimum 2026; high = upper end of student postings seen (job-aggregator, weak). U-M floor not re-verified for AY2026-27.

default_vot_usd_h.source: Computed 0.5 x $15/h (USDOT share x U-M student wage floor). Range: 0.35 x $13.73 = $4.81 to 1.0 x $15 (full wage: student who would otherwise work). Student VOT studies span roughly EUR1.4-18/h (Trieste RP/SP) and $6-23/h (US SP studies)
default_vot_usd_h.note: Dominant input; the app should show hours first and let the user set VOT; Monte Carlo over [low, high].

in_vehicle.note: All other time components are expressed as in-vehicle-minute equivalents.

walk.source: Wardman et al. worldwide meta-analysis of time multipliers (2872 multipliers, 606 studies, 52 countries, 1963-2023; indexed TRID 2026): supports reducing the conventional 2.0 to 1.75 (RP emphasis) or 1.50 (SP emphasis). USDOT guidance: walk/wait/transfer at 100% of wage vs 50% for in-vehicle => 2.0. Abrantes & Wardman (2011) UK meta-analysis: walk/wait ratio 'substantially lower than two'.
walk.note: Applies to access/egress walks of transit trips and to pure-walk trips. Bad-weather adjustment applied on top (weather.bad_day_walk_multiplier).

wait.source: Same sources as walk (Wardman worldwide meta-analysis 1.5-1.75; USDOT 2.0; Abrantes & Wardman 2011 <2)
wait.note: Applies to time actually standing at the stop (incl. outdoor exposure). Forced early arrival at destination is NOT wait; use schedule_delay_early_per_min.

bike.source: No verified cycling-time multiplier found this session; set equal to in-vehicle time
bike.note: Exercise co-benefit vs effort/exposure roughly offset by assumption. Winter cycling handled by weather; consider disabling bike on snow-cover days.

transfer_penalty_min.source: Garcia-Martinez et al. (2018) Transp. Res. A 114:52-66, Madrid SP: pure transfer penalty = 15.2-17.7 in-vehicle minutes (excluding walk/wait). Currie (2005) J. Public Transp. 8(1): review avg bus-bus transfer penalty ~22 min (range 5-50), not netting out walk/wait
transfer_penalty_min.note: Added per transfer, in in-vehicle minutes, on top of the transfer walk and wait already charged at walk/wait multipliers. Scaled below Madrid metro commuters' value because campus trips are short and UM/AAATA transfers are mostly same-stop or short walks; this scaling is our assumption.

schedule_delay_early_per_min.source: Small (1982) AER 72(3):467-479 scheduling model; Small's own bottleneck review summarizes his estimates as approx beta/alpha = 0.5 (early) and gamma/alpha = 2 (late). Wardman, Chintakayala & de Jong (2016) Transp. Res. A 94:93-111 also meta-analyse schedule-delay-early/late values
schedule_delay_early_per_min.note: DIMENSIONLESS multiplier on VOT: each minute of forced early arrival beyond arrival_buffer_min costs 0.5 x VOT/60 dollars. Early time on campus is partly usable (study), hence < in-vehicle.

bad_day_walk_multiplier.source: Physical slowdown: Fossum (winter pavement, Norway) ~+1 min/km on best winter surface, ~+2 min/km on clean ice vs bare pavement (~+8-17% at 12 min/km); computer-vision study in a cold region: speed -0.102 m/s on snow cover (~-8% at 1.3 m/s). Discomfort: 2026 preprint DCE finds per-minute WTP for time savings rises ~1.66x in rain vs sun (rain, not snow; unreviewed)
bad_day_walk_multiplier.note: A 'bad day' = day with snow depth >= 1 in (NOAA SNWD normals). Multiplies walk and outdoor wait minutes on those days; expected monthly factor = 1 + (m-1) * snow_cover_days/days_in_month * Profile.winter_aversion. Value combines ~10-15% slower walking with a modest discomfort premium; not a single-study estimate.

usd_per_outdoor_min.source: No study found that prices walking after dark in $/min. Context: Gallup (2023 release) 40% of US adults afraid to walk alone at night within a mile of home; women 53% vs men 26%. Lighting/reassurance literature (Fotios et al.) shows route avoidance after dark but no time-equivalent
usd_per_outdoor_min.note: Extra $ per outdoor minute (walking or waiting) after 22:00, scaled by Profile.late_night_weight. $0.10/min = $6/h, i.e. ~+45% on a walk minute at default VOT ($7.50 x 1.75 = $13.1/h). Wide range on purpose; show it as a user slider.

home_return_min_gap.source: Project day-tour rule (concepts/final-recommendation.md v2): go home between events only if gap > round trip + this slack
home_return_min_gap.note: Minutes of at-home time needed to make a trip home worthwhile. Kobus et al. (2015) show long-commute students visit campus fewer days but stay longer: consistent with chaining.

arrival_buffer_min.source: Project rule (final-recommendation.md v2). Theory: with schedule-delay costs beta (early) and gamma (late), the cost-minimizing on-time probability is gamma/(beta+gamma) ~= 2/(0.5+2) = 0.8 (Small 1982; Noland & Small 1995)
arrival_buffer_min.note: Deterministic buffer used with GTFS times. If ride-time noise is modeled, replace by the 80th-percentile travel time (see literature-review.md, upgrade U4).

academic_weeks_per_year.source: U-M Board of Regents, proposed Ann Arbor calendar 2026-27 (regents.umich.edu meeting 09-2025, via search extract): fall classes begin Mon 2026-08-31; 69 class days in fall and 69 in winter. 69/5 = 13.8 class weeks + ~1 week of exams/study days per term
academic_weeks_per_year.note: Weeks a student commutes on the term schedule (fall + winter, incl. exam weeks, excl. breaks). Registrar PDF not reachable; exact exam end dates unverified.
